# VisuallyHidden

Text that assistive technology reads and nobody sees: a one-pixel, clipped span taken out of the flow. It is Bootstrap's `.visually-hidden` helper, which the rest of the system already uses by class name, given a component so the caller never types the class. It paints nothing, so it takes no tokens.

Also asked as: screen reader only, sr-only, assistive text, screen reader text.

**Import:** `import { VisuallyHidden } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.stories.jsx` — Overview, NamesAControl, HiddenColumnHeaders, RoleAndId, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.mdx`

## Usage

Use `VisuallyHidden` when the words a screen reader needs are not words a
sighted person needs: the name of an icon-only button, the title of a table
column that holds only checkboxes, the count in a status message, a table
caption the layout already explains.

It renders Bootstrap's `.visually-hidden` on a `span`, which is one pixel
square, clipped, out of the flow and kept in the accessibility tree. Existing
markup that writes `className="visually-hidden"` is the same thing and can move
to the component as it is touched.

## Best practices

### Name icon-only controls. {#name-icon-only-controls}

A control with no visible words still needs a name a screen reader can say.

Do: Hidden text names the icon.
Don't: An icon-only control left unnamed.

### Add context the layout implies. {#add-context-the-layout-implies}

Sighted readers see the heading above a link; others need the words.

Do: Hidden words complete the link.
Don't: “Read more” repeated with no object.

### Do not repeat what is visible. {#do-not-repeat-what-is-visible}

Hidden text that duplicates visible text is read twice.

Do: The visible label speaks for itself.
Don't: The label echoed in hidden text.

### Hide with this, not with `display: none`. {#hide-with-this-not-with-display-none}

`display: none` and the `hidden` attribute remove the text from the
accessibility tree too, so nothing is announced.

```jsx
// Incorrect: nothing is announced.
<span style={{ display: 'none' }}>Delete session</span>

// Correct: drawn nowhere, still read.
<VisuallyHidden>Delete session</VisuallyHidden>
```

### Do not hide what a sighted person also needs. {#do-not-hide-what-a-sighted-person-also-needs}

An instruction that is invisible to people who can see is one they cannot
find. Say it to everyone, and let the field point at it.

```jsx
<p id="pw-help">Passwords must be at least 12 characters.</p>
<input aria-describedby="pw-help" />
```

### Keep it out of the focus order. {#keep-it-out-of-the-focus-order}

A hidden link or button can still be focused, and a keyboard user lands on
something they cannot see. Hide text, not controls; a skip link needs to
appear on focus.

## Accessibility

- **Announced, not drawn.** The text stays in the accessibility tree, so it is
  part of the name, description or content of whatever contains it. This is the
  difference from `display: none`, `visibility: hidden` and `aria-hidden`, which
  remove it.
- **Pair with `aria-hidden` on the visual.** An icon beside hidden text should be
  `aria-hidden="true"`, so the control is announced once, by its text.
- **Live regions.** `role="status"` makes a polite announcement when its text
  changes. Render the region before the text changes, since a region that
  appears already filled is often not announced.
- **No contrast or size to meet.** Nothing is painted, so there is no color
  requirement. The text should still be written for the ear: complete words, in
  the page's language.

## Related

- For an icon-only button, pair it with `Tooltip` so sighted people get the name too.
- For a visible label on a field, see Form.
- For a loading indicator that announces itself, `Spinner` already includes a visually hidden label.

Same group: `Accordion` · `Carousel` · `PageHeader` · `Panel` · `ScrollBar`

## Parts

1. **Span.** The only part: a one-pixel, clipped `span` of text, out of the flow, that stays in the accessibility tree and paints nothing.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. Nothing is drawn; the text is read as part of whatever contains it. |
| Hovered | None. There is nothing on screen to point at. |
| Pressed | None. There is nothing on screen to press. |
| Focused | None. It is not in the tab order; keep controls out of it. |
| Disabled | None. It has no disabled state. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Span | None. It paints nothing, so it takes no color, type or spacing tokens. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name what the control does: "Delete session". | Leave an icon-only control with no name. |
| Add only the words the layout implies: "Read more about the spring schedule". | Repeat words that are already visible. |
| Write for the ear: complete words, in the page's language. | Hide instructions a sighted person also needs. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node | — | The text screen readers announce. |
| `id` | string | — | An id other elements can point at with `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby`. |
| `role` | string | — | An ARIA role for the span, such as `status` for a live region. |
